chapter_title_en: Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ისმენდი, მოეც გონება ჩემთა ამბავთა სმენასა,
საუბართა და საქმეთა, ვითა ძლივ ვათქმევ ენასა;
იგი, ვინ ხელ-მქმნა, მოველი მისგან აროდეს ლხენასა,
და ვისგან შევუცავ სევდათა, სისხლისა ღვართა დენასა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Hearken, give heed to the hearing of my tidings, discourses and deeds such that I can scarce utter them! She who maddens me, for whom I am overpowered by melancholy, for whom flow streams of blood, from her I never expect comfort.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 310; Wardrop Stanza 300): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ინდოეთს შვიდთა მეფეთა ყოვლი კაცი ხართ მცნობელი:
ექვსი სამეფო ფარსადანს ჰქონდა, თვით იყო მპყრობელი,
უხვი, მდიდარი, უკადრი, მეფეთა ზედა მფლობელი,
და ტანად ლომი და პირად მზე, ომად მძლე, რაზმთა მწყობელი.
stanzas.english_translation: "Thou knowest, as every man knows, of India's seven kings. P’harsadan possessed six kingdoms; he was sovereign, generous, rich, bold, ruler over kings, in form a lion, in face a sun, a conqueror in battle, a leader of squadrons.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 311; Wardrop Stanza 301): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.english_translation: "My father sat on the seventh throne, king, terror of adversaries; Saridan was his name; not underhanded in the destruction of enemies, none dared offend him either openly or secretly; he hunted and made merry, careless of Fate.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 312; Wardrop Stanza 302): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ხალვა მოსძულდა, შეექმნა გულს კაეშანთა ჯარები.
თქვა: “წამიღია მტერთაგან ძლევით ნაპირთა არები,
ყოვლგნით გამისხმან, მორჭმით ვზი, მაქვს ზეიმი და ზარები;
და ბრძანა: “წავალ და მეფესა ფარსადანს შევეწყნარები”.
stanzas.english_translation: "He hated solitude; it created hosts of cares in his heart. He said to himself: 'By conquest I have taken from foes the vicinage of the marches, I have chased them forth everywhere, I am seated in power, I have pomp and might; he said: 'I will go and enjoy the favour of King P’harsadan.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 313; Wardrop Stanza 303): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ფარსადანს წინა დაასკვნა გაგზავნა მოციქულისა.
შესთვალა: “შენ გაქვს მეფობა ინდოეთისა სრულისა;
აწ მე მწადს, თქვენსა წინაშე მეცა ვცნა ძალი გულისა,
და სახელი დარჩეს ჩემისა ერთგულად ნამსახურისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "He resolved to despatch an envoy to P’harsadan; he sent a message saying: 'Thou hast the rule of all India; now I also wish to exhibit before you the power of my heart; may the glory of my faithful service remain!'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 314; Wardrop Stanza 304): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ფარსადან შექმნა ზეიმი ამა ამბისა მცნობელმან.
შესთვალა: “ღმერთსა მადლობა შევსწირე ხმელთა მფლობელმან,
რათგან ეგე ჰქმენ მეფემან, ჩემებრ ინდოეთს მჯდომელმან,
და აწ მოდი, ასრე პატივ გცე, ვითა ძმამან და მშობელმან”.
stanzas.english_translation: "P’harsadan, on hearing those tidings, made great jubilation. He sent a message: 'I, ruler of the lands, give thanks to God, because thou, a king like me enthroned in India, hast done this; now come, I shall honour thee like a brother and parent.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 315; Wardrop Stanza 305): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ერთი სამეფო, საკარგყმო, უბოძა ამირბარობა.
თვით ამირბარსა ინდოეთს აქვს ამირსპასალარობა.
მეფე რა დაჯდა, არა სჭირს ხელისა მიუმცდარობა;
და სხვად პატრონია, მართ ოდენ არა აქვს კეისარობა.
stanzas.english_translation: "He bestowed on him one kingdom well worthy of a good knight (or vassal), also the dignity of Amirbar (Grand Marshal)--the Amirbar in India is also Amirspasalar (Commander-in-Chief); when he sat as king, he was not absolute: he only lacked the overlordship, in all else he was sovereign lord.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 316; Wardrop Stanza 306): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“თვით მეფემან მამაჩემი დაიჭირა სწორად თავსა.
თქვა: “ჩემებრი ამირბარი, ნაძლევი ვარ, ვისმცა ჰყავსა!”
ლაშქრობდის და ნადირობდის, აძლევდიან მტერნი ზავსა.
და მას არა ვჰგავ ასრე, ვითა მე სხვა კაცი არა მგავსა.
stanzas.english_translation: "The king considered my father equal with himself; he said: 'I wager that no man has an Amirbar like mine.' They waged war and they hunted; they forced their enemies to make peace. I am not like him, as no other man is like me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 317; Wardrop Stanza 307): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ძე არა ესვა მეფესა და დედოფალსა მზისა დარსა,
ჭმუნვა ჰქონდა, ჟამი იყო, მით აეხვნეს სპანი ზარსა;
ვა, კრულია დღემცა იგი, მე მივეცი ამირბარსა!
და მეფემ ბრძანა: “შვილად გავზრდი, თვით ჩემივე გვარი არსა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "The king and the sunlike queen had no child, for this they were sad; a time came when the armies were seized with alarm thereat. Woe befall that cursed day when I was given (born) to the Amirbar! The king said: 'I shall rear him as my son; he is even of mine own race.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 318; Wardrop Stanza 308): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მეფემან და დედოფალმან მიმიყვანეს შვილად მათად,
საპატრონოდ მზრდიდეს სრულთა ლაშქართა და ქვეყანათად,
ბრძენთა მიმცეს სასწავლელად ხელმწიფეთა ქცევა-ქმნათად;
და მოვიწიფე, დავემსგავსე მზესა თვალად, ლომსა ნაკვთად.
stanzas.english_translation: "The king and queen took me as their child, they brought me up as lord of all the soldiers and countries, they gave me wise men to instruct me in the behaviour and deportment of kings. I grew up, I became like the sun to look upon, like a lion in mien.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 319; Wardrop Stanza 309): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.english_translation: "Asmat’h, tell me whatever thou knowest to be false in my story! When I was five years old I was like an opened rosebud; to me it appeared no labour to slay a lion--it was like a sparrow. P’harsadan cared not that he had no son.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 320; Wardrop Stanza 310): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ასმათ, შენცა ხარ მოწამე ჩემისა ფერ-მიხდილისა,
მზესა მე ვსჯობდი შვენებით, ვით ბინდსა ჟამი დილისა;
იტყოდეს ჩემი მნახავნი: “მსგავსია ედემს ზრდილისა”.
და აწ მაშინდლისა ჩემისა სახე ვარ ოდენ ჩრდილისა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Asmat’h, thou art witness of my pallor! I was fairer in beauty than the sun, as the hour of dawn than darkness. Those who saw me said: 'He is like a nursling of Eden.' My person now is but a shadow of what it was then.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 321; Wardrop Stanza 311): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე ხუთისა წლისა ვიყავ, დაორსულდა დედოფალი”.
ესე რა თქვა, ყმამან სულთქნა, ცრემლით ბრძანა: “შობა ქალი”.
დაბნედასა მიეწურა, ასმათ ასხა გულსა წყალი:
და თქვა: “მაშინვე მზესა ჰგვანდა, აწ მედების ვისგან ალი!
stanzas.english_translation: "I was five years old when the queen became with child." When he had said this the youth sighed, and weeping said: "She bare a daughter." He was like to faint; Asmat’h sprinkled water on his breast. He said: "She for whom these flames now burn me was like the sun even then.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 322; Wardrop Stanza 312): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.english_translation: "The tongue with which I now speak cannot utter the praise of her. P’harsadan sat down to announce the good news with jubilation and pomp. From everywhere came kings bringing many kinds of gifts. They gave away treasure; they filled the soldiers with presents.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 323; Wardrop Stanza 313): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ქება არ ითქმის ენითა, აწ ჩემგან ნაუბარითა.
ფარსადან დაჯდა ხარებად ზეიმითა და ზარითა;
ყოვლგნით მოვიდეს მეფენი ნიჭითა მრავალ-გვარითა.
და საჭურჭლე გასცეს; აივსნეს ლაშქარნი საბოძვარითა.
stanzas.english_translation: "The guests at the birth festivities separated. They began to rear me and the maiden; even then she was like the sun's rays augmented threefold; the king and queen loved us and looked on us alike. Now shall I utter the name of her for whom my heart is consumed by flame."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 324; Wardrop Stanza 314): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“საშობელი გაიყარა, ზრდა დაგვიწყეს მე და ქალსა.
მართ მაშინვე ჰგვანდა იგი მზისა შუქთა ნასამალსა.
ვუყვარდით და სწორად ვუჩნდით მეფესა და დედოფალსა.
და აწ ვახსენებ, ვისგან ჩემი დაუდაგავს გული ალსა!”
stanzas.english_translation: The knight swooned when he sought to mention her name. Avt’handil also wept; his fire made his heart like soot. The maiden revived (Tariel); she sprinkled water on his breast. He said: "Hearken! but this truly is the day of my death.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 325; Wardrop Stanza 315): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.english_translation: "That maiden was called by the name Nestan-Daredjan. When she was seven years old she was a gentle and wise maid, moonlike, not equalled by the sun in beauty; from her how can the heart bear separation (even if it were) adamant or forged (steel)?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 326; Wardrop Stanza 316): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მას ქალსა ნესტან-დარეჯან იყო სახელად ხმობილი.
შვიდისა წლისა შეიქმნა ქალი წყნარი და ცნობილი,
მთვარისა მსგავსი, შვენებით მზისაგან ვერშეფრობილი;
და მისსა ვით გასძლებს გაყრასა გული ალმასი, წთობილი!
stanzas.english_translation: "So she grew up, (and) I was able to go to battle. Since the king looked upon the maid as the heir to the kingship, he gave me back into the hands of my father. When I was of that age I played at ball, I sported in the lists, I killed a lion like a cat.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 10 ('Telling of his Tale by Tariel when he First Told it to Avtandil', Stanza 327; Wardrop Stanza 317): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel begins narrating his life story: how his father Saridan, King of one-seventh of India, voluntarily united his realm with King Parsadan of the other six kingdoms (reflecting Rustaveli's ideal of a centralized monarchy) in exchange for the office of Amirbar (Commander-in-Chief and Grand Admiral), and how Tariel was raised as heir by the childless King Parsadan and Queen until the birth of Princess Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“იგი ასრე მოიწიფა, მე შემეძლო შესლვა ომსა;
მეფე ქალსა ვით ხედვიდა მეფობისა ქმნისა მწთომსა,
მამასავე ხელთა მიმცეს; რა შევიქმენ ამა ზომსა,
და ვბურთობდი და ვნადირობდი, ვით კატასა ვხოცდი ლომსა.
